1.n: epic Ἠέλιος = Ἥλιος; capitalized in the text, the Sun as a person

1.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

1.n: 'the mere', water that washes a shore, used of the sea (Iliad 13.32, 24.79); here of the stream of Ocean, beside which the sun rises (Iliad 7.421–422) (Merry on 3.1)

2.n: epic/Ionic ἐς = εἰς, set between noun and adjective

'of much bronze': taken of old as 'solid, firm', like χάλκεον οὐρανόν (Iliad 17.425) and σιδήρεον οὐρανόν (15.329), by others as 'bright-flashing'; most vividly, the sky as a vault of burnished metal (Merry on 3.2); οὐρανὸν ἐς πολύχαλκον as Iliad 5.504
epic by-form of φαίνω, intransitive 'shine', in Homer only in the Odyssey (12.383, 12.385, 18.343); optative of purpose after the past ἀνόρουσε (1)

3.n: epic dat. pl. -οισι(ν); the line again 12.386

4.n: Telemachus and his crew; subject of ἷξον (5)

accusative of the place reached, with ἷξον (5); the site of Nestor's Pylos was disputed in antiquity: Strabo argued for the Triphylian Pylos, the scholia, Eustathius and Pindar (Nestor 'the Messenian', Pythian 6.35) for the Messenian, which Merry prefers (Merry on 3.4)

5.n: mixed aorist ἷξον of ἵκω (= ἱκνέομαι), + acc. of the place reached

6.n: πᾶς + μέλας 'black'; in Homer again only 10.525 and 11.33, of the black ram for Teiresias; black victims went to the powers below or to Earth (Iliad 3.103), here perhaps for the dark sea (Merry on 3.6)
κύανος 'dark blue' + χαίτη 'hair, mane': 'blue-black haired', an epithet of Poseidon; of a horse Iliad 20.224 (Merry on 3.6)

7.n: Ionic ἕδρη = ἕδρα 'seat', here a company seated together, a 'mess'; the nine answer to the nine cities of Nestor (scholia; Iliad 2.591–594), and 9 × 500 = 4,500 to the crews of his ninety ships (Iliad 2.602) at fifty a ship (Iliad 2.719) (Merry on 3.7)

8.n: contracted (προ-έχοντο): 'held before them', ready to slaughter (Eustathius), as πρὸ δὲ δούρατʼ ἔχοντο Iliad 17.355; the companies are about to begin the sacrifice (Merry on 3.8)
'in each place' (ἕκαστος + -θι); only here in Homer

9.n: = εὖτε, elided, τ → θ before the rough breathing of οἱ; 'at the moment when', the clause standing without a connective (Merry on 3.9)
sacrificial term: heart, liver, lungs, kidneys; σπλάγχνα πάσαντο as Iliad 1.464
adverbial, 'thereon', on the altar; or in tmesis with ἔκαιον (ἐπικαίω 'burn upon'), as Iliad 22.170

10.n: = δέ, in the apodosis after εὖθʼ (9)
unaugmented (= κατήγοντο); middle, of seafarers, 'put in to land', as 178: the sea seen as sloping down to the shore (Merry on 3.10)
epic ἐΐσος = ἴσος (from ϝίσϝος): of a ship 'trimmed, balanced'; the scholia gloss ἰσόπλευρος 'even-sided' (Merry on 3.10)

11.n: unaugmented (= ἔστειλαν): 'furled'; with ἀείραντες, the sail is brailed up to the yard, not lowered and stowed with the mast as at Iliad 1.433–434 (Merry on 3.11, who reports the reading σεῖσαν ascribed to Zenodotus)

11.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

11.n: in tmesis: ἐκ … ἔβαν = ἐξέβησαν; epic 3 pl. -αν

12.n: in tmesis with βαῖνʼ (ἐκβαίνω), + gen. νηός; the line as 2.416, with ἐκ for ἄν
genitive of separation with ἐκ … βαῖνʼ
= βαῖνε, unaugmented; in tmesis: ἐκ … βαῖνε = ἐξέβαινε

13.n: predicative: she spoke before he did; the feminine of the formula τὸν πρότερος προσέειπε (Iliad 5.276 and often)

14.n: 'there is need', with acc. of the person and gen. of the thing, as 1.124
contracted gen. (from αἰδόος); genitive of the thing needed, with χρή (as 1.124); here 'shyness' (Merry on 3.14)
= οὐδέ; οὐδʼ ἠβαιόν 'not even a little'

15.n: crasis of τοῦ ἕνεκα 'for this reason', explained by ὄφρα πύθηαι
root aorist (like ἔγνως) of Ionic ἐπιπλώω (= ἐπιπλέω), + acc., as ἐπιπλώσας Iliad 3.47 and ἐπιπλώς Iliad 6.291 (Merry on 3.15)
epic uncontracted 2 sg. -ηαι (= πύθῃ); subjunctive after the aorist ἐπέπλως, the purpose still being worked out (Merry on 3.15)

16.n: in an indirect question; in Homer only here and 16.306
unaugmented 2nd aorist (= ἔκυθε) of κεύθω, of burial: 'where the earth covered him' (Nitzsch, in Merry on 3.16); the simple aorist only here in Homer (reduplicated κεκύθωσι 6.303)
ὅν τινα written apart = ὅντινα, in an indirect question
aorist ἐπέσπον of ἐφέπω: πότμον ἐπισπεῖν 'meet one's fate', as Iliad 7.52; with κύθε γαῖα a kind of hysteron proteron, 'how he died and where the earth received him' (Merry on 3.16)

17.n: epic gen. -οιο; in the Odyssey only here, 181 (Diomedes) and 11.300 (Castor), in the Iliad often, mostly of the Trojans (Merry on 3.17)

18.n: short-vowel subjunctive (= εἰδῶμεν) of will: 'we mean to know', 'let us learn' (Merry on 3.18)
ἥν τινα written apart = ἥντινα, in an indirect question

19.n: infinitive for imperative; the line again, with ἵνα νημερτὲς ἐνίσπῃ, 327
emphatic, with the imperatival infinitive: you must act for yourself now (Merry on 3.19)

20.n: uncontracted future (Attic ἐρεῖ); the line again 328

20.p: verb · pf. part. mid./pass. nom. sg. masc.
20.n: perfect participle used as adjective, 'wise, sensible'

21.p: verb · pf. part. mid./pass. nom. sg. masc.
21.n: perfect participle used as adjective, 'wise, sensible'

22.n: Athena in the likeness of Mentor (2.268, 2.401)
deliberative, like ἴω: short-vowel aorist subjunctive (= προσπτύξωμαι), though the form could also be future; middle 'fold to oneself', i.e. greet, accost (cf. ποτιπτυσσοίμεθα 2.77)

23.n: epic dat. pl. -οισι; dative with πεπείρημαι
Ionic -η-; perfect middle of πειράω with the dative, 'have practised myself in' (Merry on 3.23); the form only here in Homer
epic dat. pl. -οισι(ν); 'close, well-knit', of words 'wise, shrewd'

24.n: sc. ἐστί; the infinitive ἐξερέεσθαι is its subject
subject of ἐξερέεσθαι, in the accusative with the infinitive (Merry on 3.24)

28.n: the negative of οὐ … ὀίω (27) repeated to fix it on θεῶν ἀέκητι, a familiar phrase (6.240): by litotes, 'not under the disfavour of heaven'; others punctuate οὐ γὰρ ὀίω, οὔ, σε … (Merry on 3.27); accented before enclitic σε
intransitive 2nd aorist ἔτραφον 'grew up', as Iliad 2.661; epic inf. -έμεν; Herodian took it as = τραφῆναι (Merry on 3.28)

29.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. fem.

30.n: epic gen. -οιο; θεός of a goddess

31.n: mixed aorist ἷξον of ἵκω (= ἱκνέομαι)
'gathering', the Aeolic form of ἀγορά (Eustathius), here any gathering of men, not a formal assembly (Merry on 3.31); in Homer elsewhere only Iliad 16.661, 24.141; second accent from enclitic τε
Ionic ἕδρη = ἕδρα: the seated companies of 7

33.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. pl. masc.

33.n: taken with both verbs, as if ἄλλα μὲν ὤπτων, ἄλλα δὲ ἔπειρον: 'some they were roasting, others spitting' (Merry on 3.33)
πείρω 'pierce', of putting meat on spits, as Iliad 1.465

35.n: thematic imperfect of ἄνωγα, as if from ἀνώγω

36.n: Nestor's son, still unmarried (401), seemingly the youngest of the six surviving sons, who comes sixth at 415 (Merry on 3.36); in Homer only in the Odyssey

36.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

37.n: genitive with χεῖρα: 'took the hand of both'

38.n: dat. pl. of κῶας 'fleece', spread for seats
ἅλιος 'of the sea' (ἅλς), not ἅλιος 'vain'; epic dat. pl. -ῃσι(ν)

39.n: epic apocopated πάρ = παρά; accented before enclitic τε
uncontracted dat. -εϊ; Nestor's son, who fought at Troy (Iliad 9.81), perhaps the eldest, seated next to his father (Merry on 3.36)
possessive ὅς (= ἑῷ), not the relative

40.n: in tmesis with ἐν: ἐν … ἔχευεν = ἐνέχευεν; epic aorist ἔχευα (Attic -έχεα)

41.n: uncontracted dat. -αϊ, explaining the adverbial ἐν of 40 (Merry on 3.41)

41.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.
41.n: a reduplicated present from the root of δείκνυμι: 'greet, pledge' (with the cup), as δεικνύμενος Iliad 9.196 and δειδέχατο δεπάεσσι Iliad 4.4, generally 'welcoming' (Merry on 3.41); in Homer again 18.121, 20.197 (δεδισκόμενος 15.150)

43.n: hiatus before ἄνακτι, which began with digamma ((ϝ)άναξ)

44.n: gen. of the by-form δαίτη (= δαιτός), as δαίτῃσι Iliad 10.217; genitive with ἠντήσατε

44.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

45.n: aorist subjunctive (short vowel), uncontracted -εαι (= εὔξῃ) (Merry on 3.45)
the relative, agreeing with θέμις: 'as is the custom'; the old grammarians (Herodian on Iliad 2.73) took it as an adverb = ὡς (Merry on 3.45)

48.n: infinitive in indirect statement after ὀίομαι (47): he too 'is a worshipper' (Merry on 3.48)
= χατέουσι; uncontracted; 'lack, be in need of', + gen.; Nitzsch compares Aratus, Phaenomena 4 (Merry on 3.48)

49.n: comparative of νέος; second accent from enclitic ἐστιν
abstract for concrete, = ὁμῆλιξ 'age-mate', as 364, 6.23, 22.209: 'he is my equal in years' (Merry on 3.49); + dat., predicate

50.n: crasis of τοῦ ἕνεκα 'for that reason'
a cup for drinking or for libations, the δέπας of 41; the etymology is disputed (Merry on 3.50)

51.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

51.n: unaugmented imperfect (= ἐτίθει), inflected like a contracted verb (Merry on 3.51)

52.p: verb · pf. part. mid./pass. dat. sg. masc.
52.n: perfect participle used as adjective, 'wise, sensible'
'proper': one who observes δίκη, the usage common among men (cf. 244); here in serving the elder guest first (50, 53) (Merry on 3.52)

53.n: orthotone οἷ (not the enclitic οἱ), emphatic

54.n: neut. pl. acc. as adverb: 'much, earnestly'
hiatus before ἄνακτι, which began with digamma ((ϝ)άναξ)

55.n: root aorist imperative, the opening of a prayer
epithet of Poseidon: 'holder of the earth'
'think too great', so 'grudge, refuse' (Buttmann, in Merry on 3.55); prohibitive aorist subjunctive with μηδέ; + dat. ἡμῖν and inf. τελευτῆσαι (56): 'refuse not to accomplish this for us'

56.p: verb · pres. part. mid. dat. pl. masc.
56.n: epic dat. pl. -οισι; agrees with ἡμῖν

57.n: present imperative (not the unaugmented imperfect), of a lasting gift, as δίδου (58), against the aorist δός (60) of a single act (Merry on 3.57)

58.n: epic dat. pl. -οισι; explained by σύμπασιν Πυλίοισιν (59)

59.n: genitive with ἀμοιβήν (58): 'a return for the hecatomb'; here eighty-one bulls (7–8), the word used loosely of any great sacrifice (Merry on 3.58)

60.g: when we have done the business
60.p: verb · aor. part. act. acc. sg. masc.
60.n: Ionic πρήσσω = πράσσω; singular, agreeing with the nearer ἐμέ; its object is the clause οὕνεκα … (61): 'having done what we came for'

61.n: = οὗ ἕνεκα, relative, 'for the sake of which'; its unexpressed antecedent (τοῦτο) is the object of πρήξαντα (60) (Merry on 3.61)

62.n: = ἔπειτα, 'then', resuming the act already described (Merry on 3.62)
as a seeming mortal she prayed to a higher power, as a goddess she was herself answering the prayer (Merry on 3.62)

63.n: disputed: a 'double cup', two cups set base to base (Buttmann; cf. Aristotle, History of Animals 9.40), or 'two-handled' (Aristarchus, Schliemann) (Merry on 3.63)

64.n: ὣς δʼ αὔτως 'just in the same way', = later ὡσαύτως δέ (Merry on 3.64)

65.n: comparative in form (from ὑπέρ): the outer flesh, on the carcass, as against the inner parts, the σπλάγχνα (9, 40) (Merry on 3.65)
middle, 'drew (the meat) for themselves' off the spits, as Iliad 1.466 (Merry on 3.65)

66.p: verb · aor. part. mid. nom. pl. masc.
66.n: epic -σσ- aorist (= δασάμενοι); the line again 20.280
uncontracted acc. -έα (Attic -ῆ); ἐρικυδέα δαῖτα as Iliad 24.802

67.n: tmesis (ἐξ … ἕντο): 'put from themselves'; unaugmented root aorist of ἵημι (= εἷντο)

68.n: epithet of Nestor, from Gerenia (Gerena) on the Messenian gulf, a town not named in Homer, where he was said to have been reared or to have found refuge when Heracles ravaged Pylos; some ancient lexicographers took it as 'honored' (γέρας) (Merry on 3.68)

69.n: comparative of καλός: 'more proper' than to question them before they had eaten (Merry on 3.69); second accent from enclitic ἐστι
aorist infinitive of ἔρομαι (epic present εἴρομαι)

70.n: object of μεταλλῆσαι and ἐρέσθαι (69), drawn out of the question οἵ τινές εἰσιν
οἵ τινες written apart = οἵτινες, in an indirect question
with οἵ; accent from enclitic εἰσιν
unaugmented 2nd aorist passive (= ἐτάρπησαν); + gen. 'have one's fill of'

71.n: = πλεῖτε, elided, τ → θ before the rough breathing of ὑγρά; + acc. of the way
fem. noun with neuter plural κέλευθα; ὑγρὰ κέλευθα as Iliad 1.312

72.n: ἤ … ἦ 'whether … or', a double question
κατὰ πρῆξιν 'on business', as κατὰ ληίδα (106), κατὰ χρέος 11.479 (Merry on 3.72)
Ionic πρῆξις = πρᾶξις: a trading venture, cf. πρηκτῆρες 'traders' 8.162 (Merry on 3.72)
circumflexed ἦ in the second member of a double question
perfect ἀλάλημαι with present sense, 'roam about' (as Iliad 23.74)

73.n: οἷά τε adverbial, 'as, like', with μαψιδίως ἀλάλησθε (72), on which κατὰ πρῆξιν also depends by a zeugma (Merry on 3.73); second accent from enclitic τε

'robber, pirate' (ληΐζομαι 'carry off as booty'); in Homer again 9.254, 16.426, 17.425; the question was no insult: Thucydides (1.5.2) cites the old poets' asking strangers whether they are pirates as proof that piracy was then no disgrace (Merry on 3.73)
epic ὑπείρ = ὑπέρ, lengthened for the meter
epic τοί = οἵ, article as relative; accent from enclitic τʼ

74.p: verb · aor. part. mid. nom. pl. masc.
74.n: = παραθέμενοι (apocope); middle 'stake, risk', as one lays down a pledge

74.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

75.p: verb · pf. part. mid./pass. nom. sg. masc.
75.n: perfect participle used as adjective, 'wise, sensible'

76.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
76.n: ingressive aorist: 'having plucked up courage' (Merry on 3.76)

77.n: = θῆκε, κ → χ before the rough breathing of ἵνα; unaugmented (= ἔθηκε)

77.p: verb · pres. part. mid. gen. sg. masc.
77.n: 'gone away, absent'; epic gen. -οιο; the half-line as 1.135
aorist ἐρέσθαι, which serves εἴρομαι; optative of purpose after the past θῆκε

78.n: epic subj. -ῃσι(ν) (= ἔχῃ), beside the optative ἔροιτο (77)

79.n: with κῦδος, in apposition to Νέστορ
μέγα κῦδος Ἀχαιῶν 'great glory of the Achaeans', 'he of whom the Achaeans are proud', in address: of Nestor again 202, of Odysseus 12.184 (Merry on 3.79)

80.n: epic κε + future indicative; accented before enclitic τοι; the half-line as Iliad 9.262
'tell over in order'; or aor. subj. with κε

81.n: 'lying under (Mount) Neion' (Νήϊον, 1.186), like Θήβη Ὑποπλακίη, Thebe under Placus (Iliad 6.397, the scholia): of the town, not the whole island (Merry on 3.81); two-termination; only here in Homer
epic perfect εἰλήλουθα (Attic ἐληλύθαμεν), the long stem with the short ending -μεν (Monro, Homeric Grammar §25, in Merry on 3.81)

82.n: Ionic πρῆξις = πρᾶξις 'business, matter in hand'
Ionic fem. -η; 'one's own, private', from the reflexive stem σϝε- (Curtius, in Merry on 3.82); predicate, ἐστί understood; in Homer again only 4.314 (δήμιον ἦ ἴδιον) and 20.204
two-termination, with πρῆξις: 'of the people' (δῆμος), as 2.32

83.n: 'report, tidings' of my father, as σὸν κλέος 13.415; object of μετέρχομαι (Merry on 3.83)
ἤν = ἐάν (εἰ + ἄν): 'in case, in the hope that'

84.n: subject of ἐξαλαπάξαι (85), indirect statement after φασι

85.p: verb · pres. part. mid. acc. sg. masc.

85.n: 'sack utterly'; infinitive in indirect statement after φασι (84)

86.n: object of πευθόμεθʼ (87), drawn out of the clause ἧχι ἕκαστος ἀπώλετο: 'we have heard of all the others, where each perished'

87.n: = πευθόμεθα; epic by-form πεύθομαι (= πυνθάνομαι); present where English says 'we have heard', as ἀκούω 193 (Merry on 3.87)
epic relative adverb (= ᾗ), in an indirect question, like ὁππόθι (89) (Merry on 3.87)
dative of manner, as 4.489, 15.268; elsewhere a cognate accusative, as αἰπὺν ὄλεθρον 9.303, and La Roche would read λυγρὸν ὄλεθρον here (Merry on 3.87)

88.n: uncontracted acc. -έα; 'not learned of' (ἀ- + πυθέσθαι), passive here, active at 184 ('without tidings'); in Homer only these two places; 'even his death Zeus has put beyond inquiry' (Merry on 3.88)
unaugmented (= ἔθηκε); 'made', with the predicate ἀπευθέα

89.n: = ὁππόθι, elided; epic -ππ- (= ὁπόθι), in an indirect question
intransitive perfect ὄλωλα 'be lost, perish': the tense speaks of his death as a fact (Merry on 3.89)

90.n: = εἴτε, elided, τ → θ before the rough breathing of ὅ (not εἴθε 'would that'); εἴτε … εἴτε (91) 'whether … or'
accented before enclitic γε; ὅ γε 'he', Odysseus
unaugmented 2nd aorist passive (= ἐδάμη) 'was overcome', i.e. fell
dative of the agent with the passive

91.n: 'in the midst of', as μεθʼ αἵματι Iliad 15.118 (Merry on 3.91)
in Homer the sea itself personified rather than the goddess of later legend (Merry on 3.91); only in the Odyssey (again 5.422, 12.60, 12.97)

92.n: crasis of τοῦ ἕνεκα; the line = Iliad 18.457; 92–101 again 4.322–331
= γούνατα (epic = γόνατα), elided; τ → θ before rough breathing
middle in the sense of the active; + acc.: 'come (as a suppliant) to'
epic αἰ = εἰ; αἴ κε(ν) 'in the hope that'; accent from enclitic κʼ

93.n: aorist ἔνισπον of ἐνέπω 'tell'; infinitive with ἐθέλῃσθα (92)

94.n: genitive of the source with ἄκουσας; on πλαζομένου (95) see there

95.p: verb · pres. part. mid./pass. gen. sg. masc.
95.n: middle-passive 'wander, roam'; the translation takes it with ἄλλου (94), 'from another, a wanderer'; Merry, because of the following γάρ, of Odysseus, with μῦθον: 'the story of him on his wanderings' (Merry on 3.95)
adverbial πέρι (accent thrown back): 'exceedingly', with ὀιζυρόν (Merry on 3.95)

96.n: = με, object of both participles, αἰδόμενος and ἐλεαίρων (Merry on 3.96)

96.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.
verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

97.n: 'sight' (ὄπωπα): 'how you got sight of him' (Merry on 3.97); genitive with ἤντησας; in Homer again 4.327, 9.512, 17.44

98.n: εἴ ποτε … a formula of adjuration (Merry on 3.98); accent from enclitic ποτέ
epic τοι = σοι; accented before enclitic τι

99.n: hiatus before it (originally ϝέπος); ἢ ἔπος ἠέ τι ἔργον as 4.163, word and deed almost one, 'the deed foretold in word' (Merry on 3.99)

99.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
99.n: root aorist ὑπέστην: 'undertake, promise' (the scholia: ὑποσχόμενος) (Merry on 3.99)

100.n: epic ἐνί = ἐν; after its noun, accent thrown back (anastrophe)
in apposition to the subject of πάσχετε

101.n: genitive with μνῆσαι: the plural sums up the kindnesses implied by εἴ ποτε (98) (Merry on 3.101)
aorist ἔνισπον of ἐνέπω; imperative ἐνίσπες (like σχές), not the indicative ἔνισπες (Iliad 24.388); always at the end of the verse (Merry on 3.101)

103.n: accent from enclitic μʼ; the clause never gets its apodosis, the sentence lost in the crowd of memories, and the virtual answer comes at 120 (Merry on 3.103; the scholia compare 4.204)
active 'remind', + acc. of the person and gen. of the thing

104.n: root aorist ἀνέτλην (cf. ἔτλην of τλάω): 'bore up under, endured'; in Homer again 10.327, 14.47
'not to be checked' (ἀ- + σχεῖν); μένος ἄσχετοι as μένος ἄσχετε 2.85
epic 3rd-decl. plural υἷες; in apposition to the subject of ἀνέτλημεν

106.p: verb · pres. part. mid./pass. nom. pl. masc.

106.n: 'in quest of': κατὰ ληΐδα 'for booty', as κατὰ πρῆξιν (72)
'Aeolic' optative in -ειε(ν), of indefinite frequency: 'wherever he might lead the way' (Merry on 3.106)
his raids on the cities round Troy, Iliad 9.328–329

107.n: inner object of μαρνάμεθʼ (108): 'all the fighting we did'

108.n: = μαρνάμεθα, unaugmented (= ἐμαρνάμεθα): a finite verb where strict grammar would have μαρνάμενοι, parallel to πλαζόμενοι (106) under ἀνέτλημεν (104) (Merry on 3.108)

109.n: standing alone, always Telamonian Ajax (Merry on 3.109), who died after losing the arms of Achilles to Odysseus (11.543–551)

110.n: epic case ending -φι(ν), here dative with ἀτάλαντος
'deviser' (μήδομαι); θεόφιν μήστωρ ἀτάλαντος of Patroclus also Iliad 17.477, of Priam Iliad 7.366

112.n: killed by Memnon, 'the shining son of Dawn' (4.187–188); swift of foot and brave also at Iliad 15.569–570
adverbial πέρι (accent thrown back): 'exceedingly, beyond others'
epic θείω = θέω 'run'; infinitive of respect, as ταχὺς ἔσκε θέειν 17.308 (Merry on 3.112)

113.n: ἐπὶ τοῖς 'besides these', as ἐπὶ τῇσι Iliad 9.639 (Merry on 3.113)

115.n: with the optative ἐξερέοις (116): a remote condition

232.n: βουλοίμην … ἤ (234) 'I would rather … than', as Iliad 1.117; potential optative with ἄν; the stress falls on ἄλγεα πολλὰ μογήσας (Merry on 3.232)

232.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

233.n: οἶκος with the suffix -δε 'toward'; second accent from enclitic τʼ
'of return' (νόστος): νόστιμον ἦμαρ 'the day of homecoming'; the line again 5.220, 8.466

234.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

234.n: 'at one's hearth' (ἐπί + ἑστίη), i.e. at home

235.n: = ὤλετο, τ → θ before the rough breathing of ὑπʼ; 2nd aorist middle 'perish'
= ὑπό, governing both genitives, Αἰγίσθοιο and ἀλόχοιο, with δόλῳ a dative of manner (Merry on 3.235)
epic gen. -οιο; genitive of the agent with ὑπό
possessive ὅς (= ἑῆς), not the relative
epic gen. -οιο; with ὑπό; Clytemnestra, unnamed here

236.n: epic ὁμοίιος (cf. ὅμοιος): 'common to all', as of old age Iliad 4.315 (Merry on 3.236)

237.n: dative of interest with ἀλαλκέμεν: 'ward off from'
reduplicated aorist ἄλαλκον of ἀλέξω; epic inf. -έμεν

238.n: epic 3 sg. subjunctive -ῃσι (= καθέλῃ): 'bring down, overpower'
sense uncertain: 'that lays men out at length' (τανυ- + λέχος) or 'bringing long woe' (ἀλεγ-)

239.p: verb · pf. part. mid./pass. nom. sg. masc.
239.n: perfect participle used as adjective 'wise, sensible'

240.n: μή + ἔτι, with the hortatory subjunctive

240.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. pl. masc.
240.n: middle 'be troubled, grieve': 'although we are in sorrow' (Merry on 3.240); second accent from enclitic περ

241.n: epic κεῖνος = ἐκεῖνος; Odysseus; dative of interest

242.n: = φράσσαντο, unaugmented (= ἐφράσαντο); epic -σσ-; aorist 'have determined' (Merry on 3.242)

243.n: 'search after, inquire about', + acc. of the thing
aorist infinitive of ἔρομαι (epic present εἴρομαι), + acc. of the person asked (Νέστορʼ, 244)

244.n: with ἄλλων at the end of the line: 'beyond others'; Merry (on 3.244) joins περίοιδε … ἄλλων 'knows better than other men'
'understanding, wisdom' (φρονέω); in Homer only here and 4.258
genitive with περί; others join φρόνιν ἄλλων 'the mind of other men' (Merry on 3.244)

245.n: 'thrice', standing for τρία with γένεα: 'through three generations' (Merry on 3.245); cf. Iliad 1.250–252
epic μιν = αὐτόν; subject of the infinitive; accented before enclitic φασιν
aorist middle, in Homer only here; γένεα accusative of duration; Merry (on 3.245) suspects the line

246.n: ὥς τε 'so that'; Merry (on 3.246) takes it as 'as it were': 'he seems to me as it were an immortal in look'; accent from enclitic τε
with εἰσοράασθαι: 'to me, to look upon'

247.n: aorist ἔνισπον of ἐνέπω; imperative ἐνίσπες (like σχές)

248.n: wonder that he came to such an end, rather than a request for details (Merry on 3.248)
'ruler, lord', used like an adjective; εὐρὺ κρείων 'wide-ruling'

249.n: = μήσατο, unaugmented (= ἐμήσατο); the subject is Αἴγισθος (250)

250.n: contracted acc. (= ἀρείονα), comparative of ἀγαθός: 'a man far better (than himself)'

251.n: uncontracted gen. (Attic Ἄργους); local genitive, 'in Argos', less definite than the dative, as οὔτε Πύλου … οὔτʼ Ἄργεος (21.108) (Merry on 3.251)
epic ἦεν = ἦν; the subject is Menelaus (249)
Ἄργος Ἀχαιικόν as Iliad 9.141, 19.115: Argos as the chief land of the Peloponnese, or as against Pelasgic Argos in Thessaly, Iliad 2.681 (Merry on 3.251)

252.n: = ἐπί; of extent: 'over (the world of) men'
parataxis: the clause gives the result of Menelaus' absence, 'so that he took heart' (Merry on 3.252)

252.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

252.n: reduplicated aorist, root φεν-: 'slew'; the object, Agamemnon, is understood

255.n: affirmative μέν, with no answering δέ
object of ὀίεαι, spelled out by ὥς κεν ἐτύχθη: 'this, how it would have turned out'
crasis of καὶ αὐτός: 'you yourself too', of your own thinking (Merry on 3.255)
with the aorist indicative: what would have happened (unreal past)
aorist passive of τεύχω 'make', with a neuter plural subject understood: 'how things would have turned out'; Ameis' reading ὥς περ ἐτύχθη 'just as it turned out' leaves 256 abrupt (Merry on 3.255)

256.n: unreal past condition, εἰ with the aorist indicative; the apodosis is τῶ κέ … ἔχευαν (258)
epic dat. pl. -οισι(ν); Agamemnon's halls, where Aegisthus now ruled
epic reduplicated aorist, no present: 'came upon, found'; the subject is Menelaus (257)

257.n: Menelaus, named at the end of the line
Τροίη with the suffix -θεν 'from', printed as one word

257.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

258.n: from ὁ: 'in that case', opening the apodosis of 256
epic = ἄν; with the aorist indicative ἔχευαν: unreal past; accented before enclitic οἱ
dative of interest with ἐπὶ … ἔχευαν: 'heaped over him'
'not even': no mound for him even in death

258.p: verb · aor. part. act. dat. sg. masc.
258.n: agrees with οἱ: 'for him, though dead'
'poured, heaped' (χέω): the earth of a burial mound
in tmesis with ἔχευαν (ἐπιχέω 'heap over'); χυτὴν ἐπὶ γαῖαν ἔχευαν as Iliad 23.256
in tmesis: ἐπὶ … ἔχευαν = ἐπέχευαν; epic aorist ἔχευα (Attic ἔχεα); the subject is indefinite, 'men'

259.n: 'birds of prey'; κύνες τε καὶ οἰωνοί, the fate of the unburied, as Iliad 22.354
'tear in pieces, devour' (δάπτω); κε is understood again from τῶ κε (258) (Merry on 3.259)

260.p: verb · pres. part. mid. acc. sg. masc.

260.n: uncontracted gen. (Attic ἄστεως): Mycenae; ἄστυ usually has initial digamma, neglected here as at Iliad 24.320 (διὰ ἄστεος); the variant Ἄργεος makes a difficulty of geography (Merry on 3.260)
with the aorist indicative κλαῦσεν (261): unreal past; accented before enclitic τις
feminine, with Ἀχαιιάδων (261); accented before enclitic μιν
epic μιν = αὐτόν; object of κλαῦσεν (261)

261.n: μέγα ἔργον here in a bad sense, 'a monstrous deed', as 11.272 (Merry on 3.261)

262.n: explains what follows: since we were held at Troy, Aegisthus had his way (Merry on 3.261); ἡμεῖς μὲν γάρ 'now we', as again 276 (Merry on 3.276)

262.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

262.n: epic ἄεθλος (Attic ἆθλος): the struggles of the war

263.n: = ἥμεθα: 'we sat' (at Troy), stayed on through the long war
= ἕκηλος 'at ease', safe at home while the others fought

dative of place: 'in a recess, the innermost part': either 'within Argos' at large or, with E. Curtius, Mycenae in the inmost corner of the Argive plain (Merry on 3.263); μυχῷ Ἄργεος ἱπποβότοιο also Iliad 6.152
uncontracted gen. (Attic Ἄργους); Argos in the wide sense, the land
epic gen. -οιο; the epithet suits the fertile plain rather than the 'thirsty' land at large (πολυδίψιον Ἄργος, Iliad 4.171) (Merry on 3.263)

264.n: = πολλά; adverbial 'much', in the English 'with many words'
= θέλγεσκε; iterative -σκ-, unaugmented: 'kept trying to charm, beguile'
epic dat. pl. -εσσι(ν); dative of means

265.n: ἦ τοι (= ἤτοι) with μέν, answered by ἀλλʼ ὅτε δή (269)

266.n: 'queenly', of rank and birth, not of character (Merry on 3.266)
Agamemnon's wife, named in the Iliad only at 1.113; the spelling Κλυταιμήστρη, which some editors print, connects the name with μήδομαι 'devise'
= κέχρητο, unaugmented pluperfect of χράομαι with imperfect sense, + dat.: 'was endowed with'; the half-line again 14.421, 16.398

267.n: epic apocopated πάρ = παρά: 'beside (her)', or in tmesis with ἔην (πάρειμι)

ἀοιδὸς ἀνήρ 'a singer', the noun used like an adjective with ἀνήρ, as ἰητρὸς ἀνήρ (Iliad 11.514); unnamed in Homer; later writers made him her moral guardian (Athenaeus, quoted by Eustathius) (Merry on 3.267)

268.n: Τροίη with the suffix -δε 'to', printed as one word

268.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
268.n: epic verb 'go'; participle accented like an aorist
perfect of ἔρυμαι (εἴρυμαι) with present sense, as εἰρύαται (Iliad 1.239): 'to guard, watch over', as εἴρυτο (23.229) (Merry on 3.267); not ἐρύω 'drag'

269.n: = ἀλλά; answers ἦ τοι τὸ πρὶν μέν (265)
ὅτε δή 'when at last'; accented before enclitic μιν
Clytemnestra, as the translation takes it, with Eustathius and Ameis: her scruples at last overcome; Merry prefers Aegisthus, 'bound him to his ruin', and Nitzsch took the bard (Merry on 3.269)
augmented aorist of πεδάω 'fetter' (πέδη), not a compound of ἐπί; + inf.: 'bound her to be overcome'; μοῖρα … πέδησε as Iliad 4.517, 22.5
2nd aorist passive ἐδάμην: 'to yield', as of yielding to passion (φιλότητι δαμείς, Iliad 14.353); with Aegisthus as subject, 'to be destroyed' (Merry on 3.269)

270.n: δὴ τότε 'then indeed', answering ὅτε δή (269)
with demonstrative force, 'that bard'; τὸν μέν is answered by τὴν δʼ (272)

270.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

271.n: apocope: κάλλιπεν = κατέλιπεν (κατ- assimilated to καλ-), unaugmented
epic dat. pl. -οισι(ν); dative of interest: 'for the birds'
'what one lights upon'; ἕλωρ καὶ κύρμα γενέσθαι as Iliad 17.151
infinitive of purpose or result with κάλλιπεν

272.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
272.n: ἐθέλων ἐθέλουσαν, the two participles side by side: the consent was mutual

272.p: verb · pres. part. act. acc. sg. fem.

272.n: 'led up, brought (to his house)'; ἀνάγω of carrying off a woman, as of Paris and Helen at Iliad 6.292
ὅν (possessive ὅς 'his own') with the suffix -δε 'to', agreeing with δόμονδε: 'to his own house', as 1.83

273.n: = μηρία; thigh-bones wrapped in fat, the gods' portion, burned in thanks for his success

274.n: = ἀγάλματα; 'things that delight' (ἀγάλλομαι): 'fair offerings' to the gods (Merry on 3.274)
'fastened up', i.e. hung in the temples as dedications
'woven stuffs' (ὑφαίνω): with χρυσόν they spell out what the ἀγάλματα were (Merry on 3.274); only here in Homer; second accent from enclitic τε

275.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

275.n: Merry (on 3.261) counts this μέγα ἔργον among the uses 'arduous, hard', unlike that of 261
οὔ ποτε 'never'; accented before enclitic ποτε

276.n: Nestor and Menelaus: the story now answers ποῦ Μενέλαος ἔην; (249)
ἡμεῖς μὲν γάρ, as 262, opens a new scene: 'now we' (Merry on 3.276)

276.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

277.n: Menelaus; with ἐγώ in apposition to ἡμεῖς (276)
φίλα εἰδότες 'with kindly feeling', + dat.; cf. ἀθεμίστια ᾔδη (9.189) (Merry on 3.277), ἤπια οἶδε (13.405), ἄγρια οἶδεν (Iliad 24.41)

277.p: verb · pf. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

278.n: the southern cape of Attica, in Homer only here; accusative of the goal with ἀφικόμεθʼ
Ionic ἱρός = ἱερός: holy for its cults; Merry thinks of the temple whose columns stand on Cape Colonna, or of Poseidon, invoked by seamen as Σουνιάρατος (Aristophanes, Knights 559) (Merry on 3.278)
Ionic gen. pl. -έων (Attic Ἀθηνῶν); the city for its land, Attica

280.n: possessive ὅς (= ἑός), not the relative
the 'gentle' arrows of Apollo, and of Artemis for women (11.172–173), bring a sudden, painless death, though not always in mercy: Artemis kills Ariadne (11.324) (Merry on 3.280)
epic dat. pl. -εσσι(ν); dative of means

280.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.
280.n: 'going at, assailing'; the line again 15.411; Iliad 24.759 has ἀγανοῖσι βέλεσσιν

281.n: the steering oar at the stern, a broad blade grasped 'between the hands' (μετὰ χερσί), not a tiller (Merry on 3.281); not in the Iliad

281.p: verb · pres. part. act. gen. sg. fem.
verb · pres. part. act. acc. sg. masc.

282.n: Menelaus' helmsman, in apposition to κυβερνήτην (279); named only here (the Iliad's Phrontis is Panthous' wife, Iliad 17.40)
patronymic of Ὀνήτωρ (a Trojan of that name at Iliad 16.604); only here
'excelled', + acc. of persons and inf. of respect (κυβερνῆσαι 283); cf. ἀπεκαίνυτο (8.127, 8.219)

283.n: epic acc. sg. (Attic ναῦν); object of κυβερνῆσαι
infinitive of respect with ἐκαίνυτο (282); the verb only here in Homer (κυβερνήτης 279)
with the optative: repeated action in the past
'drive hard, rush'; optative of indefinite frequency; cf. σπέρχωσιν ἄελλαι (Iliad 13.334)

284.n: = κατέσχετο; aorist middle, here passive in sense: 'was detained'

284.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.
284.n: middle 'be eager for', + gen.; second accent from enclitic περ; ἐπειγόμενός περ ὁδοῖο as 1.309 (Merry on 3.284)

285.n: = ὄφρα; purpose, with the optative after a past tense

286.n: 'he too': Menelaus set sail, as Nestor had (Merry on 3.286)

286.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

287.n: Ionic gen. pl. -άων of the plural Μάλειαι, beside the singular Μάλειαν (9.80): the southeastern cape of Laconia, notorious for storms and currents (4.514, 9.80–81, 19.186–187); 'round Malea and forget your home', a proverb in Eustathius (Merry on 3.287)
accusative of the goal with ἷξε (288)

288.n: mixed aorist ἷξον of ἵκω (= ἱκνέομαι), + acc. of the goal

288.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

289.n: = ἐπί; in tmesis with χεῦε (ἐπιχέω 'pour upon')
acc. of the masculine by-form ἀϋτμήν 'breath, blast'; elsewhere only Iliad 23.765
in tmesis: ἐπὶ … χεῦε = ἐπέχευε; unaugmented epic aorist

290.n: subject of τροφέοντο; second accent from enclitic τε
unaugmented; τροφέω, a by-form of τρέφω, only here in Homer: middle 'grew, swelled'; Merry's text reads τροφόεντα 'big, swollen', as Iliad 15.621 (cf. τρόφι κῦμα, Iliad 11.307) (Merry on 3.290)

291.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
291.n: 'parting (the fleet) in two', the two parts being τὰς μέν (291) and τὰς πέντε (299) (Merry on 3.291); διά + τμήγω, an epic by-form of τέμνω; the subject is Zeus (288)
the ships (νῆας) understood; τὰς μέν is answered by ἀτὰρ τὰς πέντε (299)
dative of the goal with ἐπέλασσεν

292.n: epic relative adverb (= ᾗ), defining Κρήτῃ: the part of Crete where the Cydonians lived (Merry on 3.292)
a people of western Crete, named among the island's peoples at 19.176; their city (not named in Homer) and the Iardanus lay on the north coast (Merry on 3.292)
a river of Crete, in the Odyssey only here; Ἰαρδάνου ἀμφὶ ῥέεθρα is the half-line of Iliad 7.135, where the river is near Pheia

293.n: accented ἔστι 'there is', opening the description of a place, as ἔστι δέ τις at Iliad 2.811, 11.711, 11.722
'smooth, sheer'; λισσὴ … πέτρη again 5.412, 10.4; ancient readers doubted whether it was an epithet or a place-name, Λισσής (Stephanus of Byzantium) (Merry on 3.293); not in the Iliad
fem. of αἰπύς 'steep'; second accent from enclitic τε
'(sheer) to the sea', running straight down into it

294.n: dative of place: 'on the verge of the territory of Gortyn', its border-land (Merry on 3.294)
the city of south-central Crete, in the Catalogue at Iliad 2.646

295.n: 'left', i.e. western: in Merry's account the western end of the range along the south coast; some take it for a small cape sheltering the harbour of Phaestus (Merry on 3.293)
'peak, jutting crag', here a headland of the coast
contracted (= ὠθέει); present of what always happens there

296.n: the city of southern Crete, in the Catalogue at Iliad 2.648
'stone, rock': a rock lying off the shore that breaks the waves, as the scholia explain (Merry on 3.293)
epic ἀποέργω (= ἀπείργω) 'shut off, keep off'

297.n: adverbial dative: 'with much ado, hardly' (Merry on 3.297)
aorist ἤλυξα of ἀλύσκω 'escape', + acc.; the subject is ἄνδρες (298)

298.n: subject of ἤλυξαν (297), held back to the start of the line: the men escaped, not the ships
epic acc. pl. (Attic ναῦς); object of ἔαξαν; second accent from enclitic γε
epic dat. pl. -εσσι(ν); 'rocks the sea breaks over', as ποτὶ σπιλάδεσσι 5.401; not in the Iliad
aorist ἔαξα of ἄγνυμι 'break' (from ϝάγνυμι); active, with κύματʼ (299) as subject: 'the waves broke the ships'

299.n: = κύματα; subject of ἔαξαν (298), with a plural verb
τὰς πέντε 'those five', the rest of the fleet
lengthened for the metre (-ειος as in εὐπατέρεια) from κυανόπρῳρος (κυάνεος + πρῷρα 'prow'), only here; elsewhere νεὸς κυανοπρῴροιο (Iliad 15.693, 9.482) (Merry on 3.299)

300.n: the land, dative of the goal with ἐπέλασσε; Αἴγυπτος is also the river, the Nile (4.477)
'brought near, drove to', + dat.; singular verb with the two subjects ἄνεμός τε καὶ ὕδωρ

300.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

301.n: accented ὥς 'so', as the text prints it; Merry would read ὡς 'while', answered by τόφρα δέ (303), as ἧος … τῆος in Menelaus' own account (4.90–91) (Merry on 3.301)
in Egypt and the lands near it

301.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
301.n: 'collecting', above all gifts, as those of Polybus of Thebes (4.125–132) and of the king of Sidon (15.117–119) (Merry on 3.301); Menelaus tells of it himself at 4.81–91

302.n: 'speaking another language' (ἄλλος + θρόος 'speech'); in Homer only in the Odyssey

303.n: οἶκος with the locative suffix -θι 'at': in Argos, while Menelaus was abroad

304.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
304.n: 'having killed'; Murray prints the line after 305, the order quoted by a scholion on Sophocles' Electra 267 and adopted by Bergk and La Roche, so that ταῦτα (303) looks back, not forward (Merry on 3.304)
unaugmented pluperfect (= ἐδέδμητο), perfect stem δεδμη- of δάμνημι 'subdue', as δεδμήατο (Iliad 3.183); not δέμω 'build', whose δέδμητο is at 1.426

305.n: two-termination adjective (with feminine Μυκήνης); epic gen. -οιο; πολυχρύσοιο Μυκήνης as Iliad 7.180, 11.46
singular Μυκήνη, usually plural Μυκῆναι; genitive with ἤνασσε

306.n: with ὀγδοάτῳ, ἔτει 'year' understood from ἑπτάετες (305) (Merry on 3.306)
dative of disadvantage with κακόν: Aegisthus
epic ὀγδόατος = ὄγδοος; Menelaus too came home ὀγδοάτῳ ἔτει, 'in the eighth year' (4.82)
predicative nominative: 'came as a disaster upon him' (Merry on 3.306)

307.n: Ionic gen. pl. -άων (cf. Ἀθηνέων 278); in the tragic legend Orestes comes from Phocis, and Aeschylus brings him to Athens only after the deed (Merry on 3.307)
in tmesis: κατὰ … ἔκτανε = κατέκτανε; 2nd aorist ἔκτανον
the slayer of Orestes' father, as 197 and 1.299

308.n: article used as relative (= ὅς); accented before enclitic οἱ

309.n: ἦ τοι (= ἤτοι), answered by αὐτῆμαρ δέ (311), like μέν … δέ

309.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

309.n: unaugmented (= ἐδαίνυ); active 'give (a feast)', + dat. of the guests
'a funeral banquet', with δαίνυ as δαινύντα γάμον (4.3) (Merry on 3.309); τάφον … δαίνυ as Iliad 23.29
epic dat. pl. -οισι(ν); the people of his kingdom

310.n: genitive with τάφον (309), 'the funeral of': Clytemnestra. Homer does not say how she died: Aristarchus saw here only that she perished with Aegisthus, and some ancient editions lacked 309–310 (scholia, Merry on 3.309)
'without strength' (ἀλκή): 'cowardly'; Aeschylus too calls Aegisthus λέοντʼ ἄναλκιν (Agamemnon 1224) (Merry on 3.310)

311.n: 'on that very day' (αὐτός + ἦμαρ); the line as Iliad 2.408, with αὐτῆμαρ for αὐτόματος 'unbidden'
accusative of respect: βοὴν ἀγαθός 'good at the war cry', the standing epithet of Menelaus and Diomedes; βοή the captain's rallying shout (Merry on 3.311)

312.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

312.n: in apposition to ὅσα: 'as freight' (Merry on 3.312)

313.n: καὶ σύ 'you too': the story of Menelaus' long absence is the warning
plural for one house; genitive with ἄπο
anastrophe: placed after its noun, accent thrown back
perfect ἀλάλημαι with present sense, 'roam about' (as 2.370); cf. δόμων ἄπο τῆλʼ ἀλάλησαι, Athena's warning to Telemachus at 15.10

314.n: second accent from enclitic τε; 314–316 again 15.11–13

314.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

314.n: epic dat. pl. -οισι(ν); plural for a single house

315.n: epic τοι = σοι; dative of disadvantage: 'devour (all) of yours'
in tmesis: κατὰ … φάγωσιν; the aorist φαγεῖν serves ἐσθίω

316.p: verb · aor. part. mid. nom. pl. masc.

316.n: 'vain, fruitless'; of disputed origin: Merry rejects the usual link with αὔτως 'in vain' and cites Düntzer's ταΰς 'big': 'impracticable' (Merry on 3.316); in Homer only here and 15.13
accusative of the way with ἔλθῃς

317.n: Ionic ἐς = εἰς; with a person: 'to (the house of)'

319.n: 'such men', no definite people: they spell out ἄλλοθεν (318), as the optative without κε shows; taken up by ὅθεν (Merry on 3.319)
